Convert brma Objects to posterior Draws Formats

Source: R/as_draws.R
as_draws.brma.Rd

Provides an interface to the posterior package for brma objects. These functions convert the MCMC samples from a fitted brma model to various draws formats supported by the posterior package, enabling the use of posterior's rich set of diagnostics and summary functions.

Usage

as_draws(x, ...)

as_draws_array(x, ...)

as_draws_df(x, ...)

as_draws_list(x, ...)

as_draws_matrix(x, ...)

as_draws_rvars(x, ...)

# Default S3 method
as_draws(x, ...)

# Default S3 method
as_draws_array(x, ...)

# Default S3 method
as_draws_df(x, ...)

# Default S3 method
as_draws_list(x, ...)

# Default S3 method
as_draws_matrix(x, ...)

# Default S3 method
as_draws_rvars(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'brma'
as_draws(x, include_auxiliary = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'brma'
as_draws_array(x, include_auxiliary = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'brma'
as_draws_df(x, include_auxiliary = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'brma'
as_draws_list(x, include_auxiliary = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'brma'
as_draws_matrix(x, include_auxiliary = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'brma'
as_draws_rvars(x, include_auxiliary = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

x

an object to convert. The brma methods expect a fitted brma object; default methods forward non-brma objects to the corresponding posterior conversion function.

...

additional arguments passed to the corresponding posterior function.

include_auxiliary

logical; whether to include the hidden intermediate parameters (see Details) in addition to the parameters shown by the default print() and summary() of the fit. Formula-random parameters retain their RoBMA semantic names in either case.

Value

An object of the corresponding posterior draws class.

Details

By default, the draws hold exactly the parameters that the default print() and summary() of the fit show (the location, heterogeneity, and moderator coefficients, the multilevel allocation rho, and the publication-bias parameters), together with the model-inclusion indicators behind the reported inclusion probabilities. The hidden intermediate parameters are added by include_auxiliary = TRUE: the latent cluster and estimate effects (gamma[k] and the GLMM theta[i]), the selection-model latent variables (eta), the GLMM nuisance base rates and rates (pi[i] and phi[i]), the random-effect variances, component SDs derived from a variance allocation, and total variance of formula-random models (for example tau2 or tau2_total), and the other backend variables listed below.

These functions are S3 generics. Their default methods forward to the corresponding posterior generics so attaching RoBMA preserves the usual posterior behavior for non-brma objects.

The following conversion functions are available:

  • as_draws: converts to the default draws format

  • as_draws_array: converts to a 3-D array (iteration x chain x variable)

  • as_draws_df: converts to a data frame with columns for iterations, chains, and variables

  • as_draws_list: converts to a list of lists

  • as_draws_matrix: converts to a 2-D matrix (draw x variable)

  • as_draws_rvars: converts to random variable objects

These methods require the posterior package to be installed. For brma methods, conversion is performed by first extracting the MCMC samples as a mcmc.list object and then using the corresponding posterior conversion function. By default, backend-private latent effects, known-V dependency factors, random-effect simulation and Cholesky factors, and prior-parameterization variables are omitted. Stable fitted coordinates such as model indicators remain available. Ordinary spike-and-slab backend slab and inclusion coordinates are omitted by default; include_auxiliary = TRUE retains them. Semantic random-effect indicators remain available as described below. Formula-random coordinates are replaced by their semantic RoBMA quantities using the same names as summaries, plots, and hypotheses, such as tau_total, tau_common, rho(...), and tau2_prop(...). A rho(...) column can contain NA draws: an original-scale correlation is undefined in draws where one of its standard deviations is zero, e.g. where an inclusion gate or a point prior sets it to zero. Summaries and hypothesis tests of the correlation use its defined draws; summaries computed from the exported draws need to handle the NA values. Random-effect SD switches are exposed as exact columns named after the standard deviation they act on, with an _indicator suffix, pairing with the semantic SD column the same way mu_x_indicator pairs with mu_x. A heterogeneity-component inclusion gate is 0/1, such as study: tau_indicator and observation: tau_indicator, and carries the inclusion state the summary reports under Heterogeneity:. An allocation-SD prior indicator, such as tau_total_indicator, records which mixture component allocated the total standard deviation and therefore takes one value per component, matching the order of that prior's components. Ordered predictor terms return their fitted totals and normalized sampled allocation shares by default, replacing their deterministic increment coordinates. Shares are normalized from the sampled Gamma primitives and remain defined when a total is zero or its inclusion event is off. Totals with point priors are exact constants for every fitted slice; fixed allocations do not create share columns. The labels come from the fitted BayesTools ordered specification, including reached factor levels and interaction slices. These quantities remain on the fitted predictor scale. Ordered-total mixture indicators and inclusion probabilities remain available, while nested slab and pseudo-prior coordinates are omitted. With include_auxiliary = TRUE, raw ordered increments and eligible total auxiliaries are also retained. Internal Gamma coordinates are never exported. as_draws_rvars() preserves allocation labels as scalar random variables and keeps ordinary vector and multi-slice total indices. If an ordered sampled parameter conflicts with an existing fitted column, conversion stops with classes RoBMA_ordered_draws_conflict and RoBMA_ordered_draws_unavailable, with the message Ordered sampled parameter '<name>' conflicts with existing fitted draws. Refit the model with the current RoBMA/BayesTools build. Missing required ordered sources stop with RoBMA_ordered_draws_unavailable and BayesTools_ordered_coordinates_unavailable, with parent class BayesTools_ordered_unavailable and the message Ordered source draws are unavailable. Refit the model with the current RoBMA/BayesTools build. Entirely fixed numeric-point terms need only the existing chain row count to materialize their declared totals. Both RoBMA ordered refit errors also inherit RoBMA_refit_required and BayesTools_refit_required. Structural point-prior coordinates are returned as exact constant columns, with chain timing taken from the fitted draw geometry. Private backend anchors are never exposed. Use include_auxiliary = TRUE to skip RoBMA auxiliary filtering; added backend variables retain their coordinate names, while public random-effect parameters retain their RoBMA names. brma_samples objects have separate methods documented at as_draws.brma_samples.
